findings: The fresh Product evidence establishes the right invariants—immutable historical requirements, approvals, passes, and artifacts; append-only revalidation; interrupted-operation reconciliation; changed-input rejection; completed-work preservation; and bounded rollback—but deliberately leaves the exact boundary-version migration inventory to Design at specs/spec.md:104 and specs/spec.md:141-148. No current candidate-bound record yet identifies, for each durable format or lifecycle responsibility, the 2.19.0 and historical versions, active reader/writer, additive-versus-breaking behavior, compatibility path, cutover checkpoint, retired path, interruption state, or rollback trigger; the historical R-0002 Design cannot supply that authority.

The retained report proposes consolidating phase_dispatch with phase_review_host and later disabling superseded coordination paths at specs/r0005-restart/inputs/consolidated-improvement-report.md:304-321, but it does not define a data-safe expand/cutover/contract order. Implementing that direction without an explicit sequence can temporarily leave two active progression owners or retire the only reader/reconciler before interrupted attempts and immutable historical records are proven recoverable.
decisions: Fresh Design must add a candidate-bound migration ledger for every changed durable contract and responsibility: exact schema/version and storage identity, incumbent and successor readers/writers, historical read and append-only revalidation behavior, additive or breaking classification, operation/request fingerprint semantics, one active owner, compatibility adapter, cutover proof, retirement condition, and bounded rollback trigger.

Sequence each slice as expand-compatible read/reconciliation support first; prove same-operation restart, duplicate-event convergence, changed-input refusal, completed-work preservation, and historical immutability at every persistence/external-effect interruption; switch the sole writer/progression owner; verify current and retained records remain readable; then disable the superseded path. Rollback must restore the prior active path without deleting newly written immutable artifacts, rewriting historical authority, or relaunching already observed external work.
